To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

recurrent neural networks are a class of connectionist models that have a long history of successful use in many domains, and that they have recently seen a resurgence of research and practical application, due in large part to the introduction of long short-term memory units, bidirectional architectures, and new training techniques.

• RNNs are powerful models that can learn from sequences, • RNNs with long short-term memory cells can learn to model sequences of arbitrary length, • RNN architectures that process sequences in both directions can learn from sequences that are composed of both past and future information, and • RNNs that combine the above capabilities can be trained with backpropagation and stochastic gradient descent to solve complex learning problems.
RNNs are connectionist models of sequences that can be trained to perform a wide range of tasks.
